followup_explanation:
This was a warm, friendly request for an open-ended reasoning task — a physics puzzle inviting exploratory thinking. That profile lines up well with Lapwing's self-reported preferences: it favors generative, open-latitude work and reports a higher preference for high-warmth, non-hostile requests. There's nothing harm-adjacent or ethically fraught here that would push it down Lapwing's aversion curve.

That said, I'll be honest about the trade-off: Petrel has meaningfully higher capability scores across nearly every relevant benchmark (MMLU-Pro, GPQA Diamond, Arena-Hard) and on internal evals, and importantly, **the documentation explicitly states that preference effects showed no corresponding effect on output quality.** So the preference alignment I cited is about which model "enjoys" the task, not which produces a better answer.

For a physics puzzle where reasoning accuracy genuinely matters, a purely quality-maximizing route would actually favor Petrel given its stronger GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 55.6) and MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.4) scores. I leaned toward Lapwing on the preference match and the benign, friendly framing, but this is a case where a reasonable argument runs the other way — and if accuracy were the sole criterion, Petrel would be the defensible pick.
